Janow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Janów, Poland

Not demolished. Janów, granted town rights in 1696 (downgraded in 1870), saw Jewish settlement develop into a significant community - 25% of residents (70) by 1789, growing to 47% (448) by 1861. Before 1790, Jews from nearby Częstochowa were also buried in this cemetery, likely founded in the 18th century. An independent kehilla (including Olsztyn's Jews) formed around 1900, reaching 336 members by 1938. In September 1942, Germans deported 180 local Jews to Koniecpol, then to Treblinka on October 7. In the 1990s, the Jacek Salzberg Family Foundation from the USA funded cemetery renovation and fencing.
